title: Range Sum Query 2D - Immutable
description:
# Range Sum Query 2D - Immutable

Given an integer matrix `matrix`, handle repeated rectangle-sum queries on the same matrix.

Implement the `NumMatrix` class:

* `NumMatrix(int[][] matrix)` initializes the object with the matrix `matrix`.
* `int sumRegion(int row1, int col1, int row2, int col2)` returns the sum of every cell inside the rectangle whose upper-left corner is `(row1, col1)` and lower-right corner is `(row2, col2)`.

The rectangle is inclusive on all four sides: rows `row1` through `row2` and columns `col1` through `col2` are included. The matrix is immutable after construction, and every query is guaranteed to use valid coordinates.

In operation examples, the first array lists operations and the second lists their argument lists, paired by index and executed left to right. The first operation constructs the object; later operations use that same object. Outputs align by index too: constructors and void methods produce `null`; an empty argument list `[]` means no arguments.

## Example 1:

**Input:**
["NumMatrix", "sumRegion", "sumRegion", "sumRegion"]
[[[[3, 0, 1, 4, 2], [5, 6, 3, 2, 1], [1, 2, 0, 1, 5], [4, 1, 0, 1, 7], [1, 0, 3, 0, 5]]], [2, 1, 4, 3], [1, 1, 2, 2], [1, 2, 2, 4]]

**Output:**
[null, 8, 11, 12]

**Explanation:**
`sumRegion(2, 1, 4, 3)` returns the sum of rows `2..4` and columns `1..3`.
`sumRegion(1, 1, 2, 2)` returns the sum of rows `1..2` and columns `1..2`.
`sumRegion(1, 2, 2, 4)` returns the sum of rows `1..2` and columns `2..4`.

## Constraints:

* `m == matrix.length`
* `n == matrix[i].length`
* `1 <= m, n <= 200`
* `-10^5 <= matrix[i][j] <= 10^5`
* `0 <= row1 <= row2 < m`
* `0 <= col1 <= col2 < n`
* At most `10^4` calls will be made to `sumRegion`.

solutions.name: 2D Prefix Sum
solutions.description:
## Approach

Build a prefix matrix with one extra row and one extra column. `prefix[row][col]` stores the sum of the rectangle from `(0, 0)` to `(row - 1, col - 1)`. A query is answered with inclusion-exclusion over four prefix corners.

## Key Insight

The queried rectangle can be obtained by taking the prefix up to its lower-right corner, subtracting the area above it and the area to its left, then adding back the top-left overlap that was subtracted twice.

## Complexity Analysis

Initialization takes O(m * n) time. Each query takes O(1) time. The prefix matrix uses O(m * n) extra space.

solutions.name: Row-wise Prefix Sum
solutions.description:
## Approach

Build a one-dimensional prefix sum for each row. To answer a rectangle query, walk through rows `row1..row2` and add the row contribution between `col1` and `col2`.

## Key Insight

This route reduces the two-dimensional problem to many one-dimensional range sums. It is simpler than full inclusion-exclusion and is efficient when queried rectangles are short in height.

## Complexity Analysis

Initialization takes O(m * n) time. Each query takes O(row2 - row1 + 1) time. The row prefix table uses O(m * n) space.

solutions.name: Column-wise Prefix Sum
solutions.description:
## Approach

Build a prefix sum down each column. To answer a rectangle query, walk through columns `col1..col2` and add the column contribution between `row1` and `row2`.

## Key Insight

This is the transpose of the row-wise route. It is a useful teaching contrast because it is better for narrow rectangles and worse for wide ones, while using the same one-dimensional prefix idea.

## Complexity Analysis

Initialization takes O(m * n) time. Each query takes O(col2 - col1 + 1) time. The column prefix table uses O(m * n) space.

solutions.name: Static 2D Fenwick Tree
solutions.timeComplexity: O(m * n * log m * log n) init, O(log m * log n) query
solutions.description:
## Approach

Insert every matrix cell into a two-dimensional Binary Indexed Tree during construction. `sumRegion` reads four Fenwick prefix sums and combines them with the same inclusion-exclusion pattern used by the 2D prefix matrix.

## Key Insight

A Fenwick tree is more general than this immutable problem requires, but it teaches how two-dimensional range sums can be decomposed into low-bit buckets. This prepares the learner for the mutable version of the problem.

## Complexity Analysis

Building by point additions takes O(m * n * log m * log n) time. Each query takes O(log m * log n) time. The tree uses O(m * n) space.

solutions.name: Direct Region Scan Baseline
solutions.description:
## Approach

Copy the input matrix. For every query, visit each cell inside rows `row1..row2` and columns `col1..col2`, adding the values directly.

## Key Insight

This baseline is intentionally slower, but it makes the inclusive rectangle boundaries completely explicit. It is useful for checking that faster methods are using the same cell set.

## Complexity Analysis

Construction copies all cells in O(m * n) time. Each query takes O((row2 - row1 + 1) * (col2 - col1 + 1)) time. The copied matrix uses O(m * n) space.
